job.title: Executive Director – Transformation Program Implementation
job.description:
Executive Director – Transformation Program Implementation

 

  • Lead a significant enterprise-wide transformation agenda, moving from strategy into execution and delivery
  • Shape the future of technology, digital, AI and business reform within a complex, purpose-driven organisation
  • Attractive salary package circa $400,000

 


About our client


Our client delivers important services and outcomes for a diverse community, operating within a complex environment where client outcomes, organisational performance and long-term sustainability are central to its purpose. The organisation is entering an important phase in the delivery of an ambitious transformation agenda. Following significant strategic design, planning and conceptualisation, the focus is now firmly on execution and delivery, supported by technology, digital capability, transformed business processes and a high-performing organisational culture.


The division in which this role leads brings together the organisation’s technology, digital and business reform agenda. Importantly, Technology Operations is an established and operational function within the division. This appointment is therefore focused on leading and optimising existing technology capability while driving the broader enterprise transformation agenda.

 


About the role


Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and operating as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the role will lead the organisation’s technology, digital and transformation agenda.


With much of the strategic design, planning and conceptualisation already well developed, the focus is firmly on execution, translating an ambitious transformation agenda into tangible outcomes across systems, processes and culture.


The role will lead major transformation programs, business process redesign and the continued evolution of digital, AI, cyber, data and technology capabilities. You will also provide vision, leadership and governance across IT strategy, technology plans and architecture, ensuring these capabilities remain aligned with organisational priorities and industry best practice.


Working collaboratively with the CEO and executive colleagues, the successful candidate will contribute to whole-of-organisation leadership and help create alignment around shared transformation priorities and outcomes.


 

About You


You are an accomplished executive leader with extensive experience across technology, digital and enterprise transformation, with a demonstrated track record of delivering complex, cross-functional organisational initiatives and transformation programs. You bring highly developed strategic, analytical and commercial capability, with the judgement and delivery focus required to translate strategy into implementation and maintain momentum through complex delivery.


You will bring many years of significant experience leading an information technology and transformation function, including digital capability, strategic planning, technology operations, applications, platforms and infrastructure. You will be comfortable providing executive leadership across technology while maintaining a broader enterprise perspective. Importantly, this opportunity requires more than technical expertise. You will be a collaborative and constructive enterprise leader, able to build trusted relationships at CEO, Board and executive level, navigate complexity, lead specialist teams and create alignment across diverse stakeholders.


You will bring energy, ambition and a genuine appetite for delivery, together with the resilience and adaptability required to lead a significant transformation agenda.

job.title: Board Director - headspace
job.description:
Board Director – headspace


  • Help shape the future of youth mental health through national Board leadership
  • Bring more than governance credentials - bring purpose, perspective and genuine connection
  • Contribute to a highly respected national organisation, with future Chair succession potential

 


About headspace


headspace National Youth Mental Health Foundation is a national organisation dedicated to improving the mental health and wellbeing of young people across Australia. Through its national network, partnerships, advocacy and sector leadership, headspace delivers programs and services to support the mental health and wellbeing of young people and communities.


As the national organisation, headspace National operates within a complex operating environment spanning mental health, primary care, community and vocational support services, government, research and diverse communities across metropolitan, regional, rural and remote Australia. The organisation delivers a range of national programs through headspace centres, schools, universities, and online such as eheadspace, telepsychiatry and Work and Study Online. Central to its approach is an understanding that young people’s experiences are shaped by identity, culture, community, geography and broader social circumstances.


headspace has many expansion plans over the next three years with 56 new or expanded services and an exciting digital roadmap to reach more young people experiencing a difficult time. The organisation has a deep commitment to the social and emotional wellbeing of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and is guided by a First Nations led cultural strategy and cultural governance.



About the Roles


headspace is seeking to appoint two experienced Non-Executive Directors who bring strong Board capability and, importantly, a compelling connection to headspace’s purpose, young people and the communities it serves. Both appointments will contribute across the full Board agenda and support longer-term Board renewal and potential Chair succession.

 


Board Director


This appointment is an opportunity to bring a distinctive and contemporary voice to the headspace Board. The successful Director will bring genuine connection, insight and credibility with young people and one or more communities or issues shaping their lives today, together with the judgement and governance maturity to contribute across the full Board agenda.


That connection may come through lived experience, community leadership or professional experience across areas such as First Nations, LGBTQIA+, multicultural or multifaith communities, young men, disadvantage, homelessness, AOD, family violence, disability, or regional and remote Australia. The Director is not expected to represent any particular community, but to bring authentic, contemporary insight grounded in genuine connection.


 

About You


Your Board CV matters. But your reason for wanting to join headspace matters more. You will bring the judgement, curiosity and governance maturity expected of a national Director, together with a genuine and contemporary connection to headspace’s purpose, young people and the communities it serves.


You will listen well, challenge constructively and contribute beyond your particular area of expertise. Your credibility may come through lived experience, community connection, professional leadership or a combination of these - but it will be authentic and relevant.


Across both appointments, we are looking for a clear and compelling answer to: Why headspace? Why this Board? Why now?

 


How to Apply


Interested applicants are invited to submit:


  • A current curriculum vitae
  • A brief cover letter outlining your interest in the appointment and, importantly, why headspace and why now


We encourage applicants to go beyond Board and professional credentials and tell us what connects you to headspace, young people and the communities it serves. We are interested in your motivation, perspective and the contribution you believe you can genuinely make to the Board.

 


Organisational Requirements

Successful candidates will be required to hold or obtain:

  • A valid Working with Children Check
  • A current National Police Check
  • Australian Citizenship, Permanent Residency or a valid Australian work permit/visa
